title: Protocol for generating a human iPSC-derived tri-culture model to study interactions between neurons, astrocytes, and microglia
author: Lish, Galle, et al.

steps.title: Transduce hiPSCs and create cryostocks
steps.instruction: Transduce hiPSCs with TetOn‑NGN2 and rtTA viruses for neurons, and with TetOn‑Sox9, TetOn‑Nfib and rtTA viruses for astrocytes; after establishing stable lines, freeze immature neurons (Day 4), astrocytes (Day 8) and microglia (Day 20) as cryopreserved stocks.

steps.title: QC thawed stocks before tri‑culture
steps.instruction: Thaw a test vial of each cryostock, plate in a test culture, and perform immunocytochemistry at the differentiation endpoint: neurons – NeuN and βIII‑tubulin (Tuj1); astrocytes – GFAP and CD44; microglia – IBA1 and P2RY12; assess proliferative contamination with Ki67. Confirm differentiation efficiency > 95 % and absence of proliferative cells before using the main stocks.

steps.title: Prepare Matrigel‑coated plates (optional)
steps.instruction: Coat plates with Matrigel in advance; if not used the same day, add PBS to prevent evaporation, seal with parafilm, and store at 4 °C for up to 10 days.

steps.title: Thaw and resume differentiation of each lineage
steps.instruction: Thaw the Day 4 neuron, Day 8 astrocyte and Day 20 microglia stocks and continue their respective differentiation protocols as described in Zhang et al., Lagomarsino et al., Canals et al., Lee et al., Abud et al., McQuade et al., and Chou et al.

steps.title: Replate astrocytes onto neurons (Day 20 → Day 22)
steps.instruction: Prepare astrocyte replating media by supplementing Maturation Base Media with 5 µg/mL N‑acetylcysteine, 5 ng/mL heparin‑binding EGF‑like GF, 10 ng/mL CNTF, 10 ng/mL BMP4, 500 µg/mL dbcAMP, 2.5 µg/mL doxycycline, 10 ng/mL GDNF, 10 ng/mL BDNF, 1:50 B27, and 10 µM ROCK inhibitor. Remove conditioned media from Day 20 astrocytes, wash the 10 cm plate with 3–4 mL PBS, add room‑temperature (20‑22 °C) diluted Accutase (1 part Accutase : 3 parts PBS + 10 µM ROCKi), incubate 37 °C for 5–8 min until cells lift, wash with PBS to collect remaining cells, count, centrifuge 220–300 × g for 5 min, resuspend the pellet in replating media, gently remove all media from the Day 22 neuron cultures, and plate astrocytes directly onto the neurons at ~47 000 cells/cm² (add media with astrocytes dropwise, feeding one well at a time). If only astrocyte‑neuron co‑culture is desired, continue using the same Maturation Base Media without switching to triple‑culture medium.

steps.title: Replate microglia onto co‑culture (Day 21 → Day 23/41)
steps.instruction: Twenty‑four hours after astrocyte replating, prepare triple‑culture medium by supplementing BrainPhys (STEMCELL Technologies) with SM1, 25 ng/mL M‑CSF, 100 ng/mL IL‑34, 50 ng/mL TGF‑β1, 100 ng/mL CX3CL1, and 100 ng/mL CD200. Collect conditioned media (containing floating cells) from the astrocyte‑neuron wells into conical tubes, add 1 mL PBS to each well, incubate at 20‑22 °C for 10–15 min, transfer the PBS wash to the same tubes, repeat if cells remain attached, centrifuge 220–300 × g for 5 min, resuspend and combine all pellets in 1 mL triple‑culture medium, count, adjust volume with triple‑culture medium as needed, gently remove all media from the astrocyte‑neuron cultures, and plate Day 41 microglia directly onto the Day 23 neurons and Day 21 astrocytes at ~42 000 cells/cm² (add media with microglia dropwise, feeding one well at a time).

steps.title: Maintain triple cultures
steps.instruction: Perform half‑media changes every 3 days using the same BrainPhys‑SM1 triple‑culture medium (25 ng/mL M‑CSF, 100 ng/mL IL‑34, 50 ng/mL TGF‑β1, 100 ng/mL CX3CL1, 100 ng/mL CD200).

steps.title: Experimental use and final media change
steps.instruction: Use the triple cultures for experiments 3–12 days after microglia addition. Schedule a full media change at least one full‑media‑change interval (48 h) before any media collection for analysis to minimize residual factors.

description: Before initiating astrocyte and neuron differentiations, hiPSCs must be transduced with specific viral constructs. For neurons, TetOn-NGN2 and rtTA viruses are required, while astrocyte differentiation necessitates TetOn-Sox9, TetOn-Nfib, and rtTA viruses. Once the transduced hiPSC lines are established, cryopreserved stocks of immature neurons (Day 4), astrocytes (Day 8), and microglia (Day 20) should be prepared. Basic iPSC passaging, maintenance, and freezing skills are assumed. In practice, there are three key stages to prepare for tri-culture. (1) Transduction and cell banking: Establish transduced iPSC lines and generate frozen stocks of each lineage. (2) Differentiation: Produce neurons, astrocytes, and microglia following established protocols (Zhang et al. and Lagomarsino et al.3,4 for neurons, Canals et al. and Lee et al.5,6 for astrocytes, and Abud et al., McQuade et al., and Chou et al.7,8,9 for microglia). (3) Assembly of tri-culture: Thaw cryopreserved cells and combine them for co-culture. Although the induced neuron (iN), astrocyte (iA), and microglia (iMG) differentiation methods are not unique to this protocol, we included detailed steps here for completeness and to facilitate reproducibility. If one is already experienced with generating and banking these cell types, you may skip directly to the tri-culture generation section. Before using any cryopreserved cell stock in downstream tri-culture assembly, a vial should be thawed and plated in a test culture to assess differentiation efficiency and cellular identity. Perform immunocytochemistry (ICC) at each differentiation endpoint to ensure differentiation efficiency exceeds 95% and that there is no evidence of a contaminating proliferative population. For neurons, use antibodies against NeuN and βIII-tubulin (Tuj1); for astrocytes, use GFAP and CD44; and for microglia, use IBA1 and P2RY12.
